arxiv-2101-06075.title: Frustration, strain and phase co-existence in the mixed valent hexagonal iridate Ba 3 NaIr 2 O 9
arxiv-2101-06075.creator: Charu Garg, Antonio Cervellino, Sunil Nair
arxiv-2101-06075.description: Abstract Using detailed synchrotron diffraction, magnetization, thermodynamic and transport measurements, we investigate the relationship between the mixed valence of Ir, lattice strain and the resultant structural and magnetic ground states in the geometrically frustrated triple perovskite iridate Ba 3 NaIr 2 O 9 .

arxiv-2204-10492.title: Gravity aided navigation using Viterbi map matching algorithm
arxiv-2204-10492.creator: Wenchao Li, Christopher Gilliam, Xuezhi Wang, Allison Kealy, Andrew D. Greentree, Bill Moran
arxiv-2204-10492.description: Abstract In GNSS-denied environments, aiding a vehicle’s inertial navigation system (INS) is crucial to reducing the accumulated navigation drift caused by sensor errors (e.g. bias and noise). One potential solution is to use measurements of gravity as an aiding source. The measurements are matched to a geo-referenced map of Earth’s gravity in order to estimate the vehicle’s position.

arxiv-2304-03787.title: Fourier expansion in variational quantum algorithms
arxiv-2304-03787.creator: Nikita A. Nemkov, Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Aleksey K. Fedorov
arxiv-2304-03787.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nikita A. Nemkov, Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Aleksey K. Fedorov. The Fourier expansion of the loss function in variational quantum algorithms (VQA) contains a wealth of information, yet is generally hard to access. We focus on the class of variational circuits, where constant gates are Clifford gates and parameterized gates are generated by Pauli operators, which covers most practical cases while allowing much control thanks to the properties of stabilizer circuits.

arxiv-2310-16056.title: Cortical Functional architectures as contact and sub-Riemannian geometry Thanks: Giovanna Citti, Dipartimento di Matematica, University of Bologna Alessandro Sarti, CNRS-CREA, Ecole Polytechnique, Paris
arxiv-2310-16056.creator: Giovanna Citti, Alessandro Sarti
arxiv-2310-16056.description: Abstract . In the paper [ 67 ] , Jean Petitot together with the authors of the present paper describe the functional geometry of the visual cortex as the symplectization of a contact form to describe the family of cells sensitive to position, orientation and scale.

arxiv-2411-11161.title: MPLite: Multi-Aspect Pretraining for Mining Clinical Health Records Thanks: 2 Equal contribution as co-first authors. Thanks: 1 Corresponding author
arxiv-2411-11161.creator: Eric Yang 2, Pengfei Hu 2, Xiaoxue Han, Yue Ning 1
arxiv-2411-11161.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Eric Yang 2, Pengfei Hu 2, Xiaoxue Han, Yue Ning 1. The adoption of digital systems in healthcare has resulted in the accumulation of vast electronic health records (EHRs), offering valuable data for machine learning methods to predict patient health outcomes. However, single-visit records of patients are often neglected in the training process due to the lack of annotations of next-visit information, thereby limiting the predictive and expressive power of machine learning models.

arxiv-2506-07361.title: What holes in superconductors reveal about superconductivity
arxiv-2506-07361.creator: J. E. Hirsch
arxiv-2506-07361.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by J. E. Hirsch. We consider a type I superconducting body that contains one or more holes in its interior that undergoes a transition between normal and superconducting states in the presence of a magnetic field. We argue that unlike other thermodynamic systems that undergo first order phase transitions the system cannot reach its equilibrium thermodynamic state, and that this sheds new light on the physics of the Meissner effect.

britannica-1911-taunton.title: Taunton (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-taunton.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-taunton.description: Article 'Taunton' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. market town of Somersetshire, England, on the river Tone, 163 m. of London by the Great Western railway. Standing in the beautiful valley of Taunton Dene, the town is chiefly built on the south side of the river. Its three main streets, broad and regular, converge upon a triangular space called the Parade, where there is a market cross.

pmc-10668688.creator: Natalia A. Volkova, Michael N. Romanov, Alexandra S. Abdelmanova, Polina V. Larionova, Nadezhda Yu. German, Anastasia N. Vetokh, Alexey V. Shakhin, Ludmila A. Volkova, Dmitry V. Anshakov, Vladimir I. Fisinin, Valeriy G. Narushin, Darren K. Griffin, Johann Sölkner, Gottfried Brem, John C. McEwan, Rud
pmc-10668688.description: Simple SummaryArtificial selection has been applied to domesticated birds for many decades. More recently, this selection has made use of so-called single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers—simple variants in a DNA sequence. These SNPs can be used for whole-genome screening to detect the unique traces of areas of the genome that are subject to selection.

pmc-11583632.title: Complicated grief following the perinatal loss: a systematic review
pmc-11583632.creator: Xi Zhang, Ye Chen, Meizhen Zhao, Mengmei Yuan, Tieying Zeng, Meiliyang Wu
pmc-11583632.description: BackgroundPerinatal loss is a severe stressor that usually triggers distressing symptoms of acute grief. Moreover, acute grief can worsen with time and become a chronic debilitating state known as complicated grief. However, there is a lack of comprehensive reviews on this topic. This systematic review aims to synthesize the existing literature on complicated grief following the perinatal loss.

pmc-12501246.title: Correlation between stress hyperglycemia ratio and risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome in patients with sepsis: a MIMIC-IV cohort study
pmc-12501246.creator: Xianwei Jin, Wei Deng, Qiaoling Weng, Fen Liu, Jia Min
pmc-12501246.description: This study aimed to investigate the association between stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) and the risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) in patients with sepsis. Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care - IV database in this retrospective cohort study. Participants were stratified into four groups based on the interquartile range of SHR.

This study investigated two marine carnivorous species with distinct fat deposition characteristics: the golden pompano (Trachinotus ovatus), which stores lipid in the liver and muscle, and the spotted sea bass (Lateolabrax maculatus), which primarily stores fat in the abdominal adipose tissue. pmc-13017337.title: Association between triglyceride glucose- systemic immune inflammation index and deep venous thrombosis in fresh fracture patient: a real-world retrospective study
pmc-13017337.creator: He Chen, Ke Chen, Xuewen Xie, Mei Lin, Weidan Yuan, Shiyun Luo
pmc-13017337.description: BackgroundCurrently, systemic inflammation indices and insulin resistance are both recognised as high-risk factors for venous thromboembolic diseases. However, there is a lack of research on the relationship between the triglyceride-glucose-systemic inflammation index (TyG-SII) and the risk of lower limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in populations with traumatic fractures.

pmc-13155246.title: Rotenone Inhibited Osteosarcoma Cell Growth Through USP47-Induced Decreases in FEN1 Stability and DNA Integrity
pmc-13155246.creator: Zhen Li, Xiang Ma, Hengwei Ma, Bao Chen, Kun Jiang, Ziqiang Zhu, Jianqiang Wang, Baoqing Wang, Yunqing Wang, Suwei Dong
pmc-13155246.description: BackgroundOsteosarcoma (OS) is the most prevalent primary malignant bone tumor in children. We previously showed that rotenone suppressed OS cell metastasis. However, its effects on OS cell growth and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. The purpose of this study was to investigate the role of rotenone in OS and identify its direct target.

pmc-13280739.title: Dual Metabolic Inhibition by Berberine and Glutor Triggers AMPK/JNK-Dependent DNA Damage in Cancer Cells
pmc-13280739.creator: Meina Shi, Chengming Wei, Dayuan Zheng, Dongfan Yang, Tong Chu, Shaokui Liang, Lu Yang, Kuanyun Zhang, Yanchao Yang, Wenzhe Ma
pmc-13280739.description: Metabolic reprogramming is a key adaptive feature of malignant tumors and often leads to the failure of therapeutic strategies targeting a single metabolic pathway. In this study, we investigated the antitumor activity of combining berberine (BBR), a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor, with Glutor, a pan-glucose transporter inhibitor that blocks glucose uptake across multiple GLUT isoforms.

pmc-13321470.title: Pre-delivery anaemia and associated factors among women in Kikuube District, Uganda: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13321470.creator: Julius Businge, Miisa Nanyingi, Mathias Lwenge, Juliet Ndibazza, Rovina Alimpa, David Agaroi, Scovia Mbabazi
pmc-13321470.description: IntroductionAnaemia in pregnancy is a global public health concern, especially in low and middle-income countries, where it is linked to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Despite various antenatal care interventions to prevent anaemia in pregnancy, a considerable proportion of pregnant women still present with anaemia at delivery.

pmc-13599307.title: When PSMA is not enough: the diagnostic blind spots of PSMA PET/CT and the added value of [¹⁸F]FDG in high-risk prostate cancer: dual-tracer cohort study
pmc-13599307.creator: Efrah Ahmed Ibrahim, Eray Alper
pmc-13599307.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposePSMA PET/CT has transformed prostate cancer management, yet its diagnostic utility is not absolute. It fails to detect PSMA-suppressed disease variants, including treatment-induced neuroendocrine prostate cancer (t-NEPC) and dedifferentiated tumors, and is inherently blind to second primary malignancies (SPMs).

pmc-13676482.title: Relative muscle mass and grip strength as complementary correlates of metabolic syndrome: a nationwide DXA-based study of Korean adults
pmc-13676482.creator: Eun Young Lee, Hyun Min Kim
pmc-13676482.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeBoth muscle mass and strength relate to metabolic health, but their separate contributions to metabolic syndrome (MetS) are unclear. Using the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) with concurrent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)–based appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM) and handgrip strength (HGS), we examined the independent associations of relative muscle mass and HGS with MetS in Korean adults aged ≥40 years.MethodsWe analyzed 3033 adults from KNHANES. ASM/body weight (ASM/BW) and HGS/body weight (relative HGS) served as primary indicators.
